item.text: The script syntax is clean. The first serving check raced the local server startup, so I’m rerunning that check with the server held open long enough to answer; no code change is needed for that timing hiccup.

This sandbox blocks opening local network sockets, so a live HTTP check isn’t available here. I’m substituting an offline HTML parse; the browser code itself already passed JavaScript syntax validation.

item.command:

from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path

class Checker(HTMLParser):
    def error(self, message):
        raise ValueError(message)

source = Path('index.html').read_text()
parser = Checker()
parser.feed(source)
parser.close()
assert '<title>One quiet minute</title>' in source
assert 'prefers-reduced-motion' in source
print(f'HTML parsed successfully ({len(source):,} bytes)')
PY"
